ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as consolidated and amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing a Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), creating Article 15-1 et seq. of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and the company accounting and annual accounts; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 March 2019 on the practical arrangements of the Register of Beneficial Owners; Law of 25 March 2020 amending the AML/CFT legal framework and implementing EU Directive 2018/843 (5th Anti-Money Laundering Directive).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority of the respective country of origin

Power of attorney for the incorporation agent or appointed manager, where applicable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the Luxembourg Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs (MFA) consolidated sanctions list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU Council consolidated financial sanctions list, OFAC SDN list and all applicable EU autonomous restrictive measures; enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons (PEPs) covering a 12-month look-back, independent source-of-wealth documentation, management approval of onboarding, and ongoing transaction monitoring; immediate reassessment upon any adverse media alert or hit against domestic Luxembourg PEP, foreign PEP, or international organization PEP.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – eRegistre online portal (www.lbr.lu / www.lbr.lu/rcs)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official register language for the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) is French; the proposed name must be written in Latin script and where the name originates in a non-Latin alphabet, a transliteration into French, German or Luxembourgish is mandatory; the name must comply with Luxembourg orthographic conventions and must not be contrary to ordre public, good morals, or be misleading as to the legal form or the reglemented nature of the business.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection of a proposed name by the Luxembourg Business Registers, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registrar of the Trade and Companies Register within 15 calendar days of the rejection notice. If the Registrar maintains the refusal, the applicant may file an administrative appeal before the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg, chambre du conseil) within one month of the written refusal; the appeal must be lodged by a Luxembourg-licensed advocate and may be further appealed to the Court of Appeal of Luxembourg within six weeks. The submission must include a certified copy of the proposed articles of association, the original rejection notice, and proof of deposit of the publication draft where applicable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office and administrative domiciliation arrangements are legally permissible for an SCSp under the Law of 31 May 1999 on the domiciliation of companies, provided the domiciliation agent is an approved Luxembourg commercial company subject to professional standards. However, for the manufacture and sale of turbine-driven critical care invasive ventilators, a pure virtual office is not appropriate: licensing, VAT registration, conformity assessment, clinical vigilance, and liability exposure require a substantive Luxembourg operational presence, including a physical registered office, technical records premises, and authorised personnel.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High and quantified at 55% within the first fiscal year, because the manufacture of invasive ICU ventilators (ISIC 3250 / NAICS 339112) is a regulated medical devices activity subject to unannounced inspections by the Luxembourg Ministry of Health, the Luxembourg Inspectorate of Labour and Mines (ITM), and the European conformity assessment authorities, in addition to tax substance verification by the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 12 July 2013 on the Special Limited Partnership (SCSp) as amended, notably Articles 1-3 (formation), 4-7 (partner liability), 8-10 (management and representation), 11-15 (capital and contributions); Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (as amended) for residual corporate governance; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 September 2011 on the Commercial Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Partnership Agreement (Convention de Société) and RCS registration declaration (Formulaire G)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal capital; paid-up capital is determined by the partnership agreement. Contributions may be in cash, in kind, or in services (services not constituting share capital for creditor protection). No escrow account is statutorily required; however, for banking AML purposes, contributions must be transferred or credited to a bank account opened in the partnership's name.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF THE SCSp: RESOLVED, that the General Partner, acting as the statutory management body of the Société en Commandite Spéciale (the 'Partnership'), hereby: (i) accepts the subscription and payment of Partnership Interests by each Initial Partner in accordance with the Partnership Agreement, aggregating EUR 100,000 in cash; (ii) adopts the Partnership's registered office at [address in Luxembourg] effective immediately; (iii) appoints [Name] as General Partner/Gérant and [Name] as Chief Operating Officer with authority to execute and file all incorporation, tax and licensing documents; (iv) opens bank accounts and engages professional advisers as required. This resolution is effective upon signature and cannot be revoked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary (if notarization required) or the partners themselves for private deed; Luxembourg civil-law notaries competent within the Grand Duchy.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SCSp partnership agreement (convention de société) in English or French with Luxembourg law as governing law. The deed must state the name, registered office, object, identity and powers of general partner(s) and limited partners, profit-sharing, capital contributions, management structure, and duration. Execute by all partners. If a partner contributes real estate or the partnership becomes regulated or listed/traded, notarization is mandatory; otherwise a private deed suffices.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all partners
Power of attorney if signatory acts by proxy
Proof of residential or registered address of each general partner
Draft partnership agreement
Project description and registered office address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notarized deed is refused due to incomplete or unlawful provisions, rectify the text and renotarize. If a private deed is challenged, amend via a subsequent deed and ensure all partners consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via MyGuichet.lu / e-RCS platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form G (request for registration) to the RCS, accompanied by the partnership agreement, proof of identity of the general partner(s), and a declaration of the registered office. Filing may be made electronically or physically at the RCS counter. Once approved, the RCS assigns a registration number (numéro d'immatriculation) and issues an RCS certificate.
required_dossiers: Form G – request for registration
Partnership agreement (certified authentic copy if notarized)
Declaration of acceptance by the custodian of accounts, if applicable
Identity documents of the general partner(s) and managers
Proof of powers of attorney for filers
Proof of registered office address (lease or consent of owner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the application, respond substantively within 15 calendar days, correcting any omissions in the Form G or the agreement, and resubmit electronically without additional fee unless changes are substantive.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the electronic company gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the RCS automatically transmits the incorporation data for publication in RESA. The published entry contains the legal form, name, registered office, object, and identification of the general partner(s) and authorized managers. Irrespective of any automatic publication, the partnership should verify the entry and, if necessary, file a rectification request.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate or extract
Copy of the rectification request, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains inaccuracies, file a written rectification request with the RCS; the RCS will issue a corrective publication. Third-party reliance on an erroneous entry may be cured by a subsequent official correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration, national identification number, and social security formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCS automatically transmits the completed registration to the AEDT, which assigns the national tax identification number (numéro d'identification). The partnership must verify receipt and completeness of this assignment. If employing staff, register with the CCSS for social security. Apply for a VAT number if the partnership will perform taxable economic activities in Luxembourg, or confirm exemption under the small business regime before any invoicing.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate
Bank account details (IBAN and BIC)
Description of planned taxable activities
Lease agreement or proof of registered office
Employment declarations (if staff are hired)
VAT application form (Formulaire A) or self-verified exemption
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax number is not issued within the projected SLA, contact the AEDT and provide the RCS certificate to expedite processing. For VAT, if the application is delayed, file a reminder and follow up by e-mail or in person; any refusal may be appealed to the Director of the AEDT.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit and medical device manufacturer authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction générale de l'industrie; Ministère de la Santé – Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for the business establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011, using MyGuichet.lu or the Ministry of Economy, providing proof of professional capacity, good character, and suitable premises. Simultaneously notify the Ministry of Health of the medical device manufacturing activity (turbine-driven critical-care ventilators) as required by Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR), and obtain the manufacturer notification/registration number. The manufacturing site must have implemented ISO 13485 and relevant technical files.
required_dossiers: Identity document and criminal record extract for each applicant/manager
Professional diploma or certificate of competence for manufacturing activity
Proof of registered office and manufacturing premises
Valid quality management system certificate (ISO 13485)
Technical file for the invasive mechanical ventilator (Class IIb or Class III)
Declaration of Conformity under Annex IX or Annex XI of EU MDR 2017/745
Evidence of clinical evaluation summary and post-market surveillance plan
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment permit is refused, file a reasoned appeal with the Ministry of Economy within 30 days; further administrative appeal to the Luxembourg administrative court within 3 months. For MDR notification, if the dossier is incomplete, supplement with the requested technical data within the given deadline; any rejection is appealable under national administrative procedure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Environmental permit, fire safety, and occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'environnement; Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an environmental permit application (autorisation environnementale) for the production and assembly premises under the amended Law of 19 March 2013 and the Grand-Ducal Regulation on classified establishments. Submit the fire safety dossier to CGDIS for certification of access, extinguishers, and evacuation plans. Before commencement of operations, request an occupational health and safety inspection from ITM covering machinery, electrical installations, and indoor emissions.
required_dossiers: Site plan with dimensions and escape routes
Description of industrial processes and waste streams
Waste and wastewater management declarations
Fire safety plans, alarms, extinguishers, and access routes
Structural load calculations for heavy equipment or high racks
Preventive maintenance schedule for mechanical and electrical systems
Personal protective equipment (PPE) assessment and training records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the environmental permit is denied or conditioned with onerous restrictions, submit a technical justification for reduced classification or amended conditions; appeal the decision to the administrative court within 3 months. Fire safety and occupational inspection remarks must be remedied on site and a revised dossier resubmitted to the respective authorities.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economy – Directorate General for Industry (Direction de l'industrie) in consultation with the Ministry of Health – Division of Pharmacy and Medicines (Division de la Pharmacie et des Médicaments)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) and Medical Device Manufacturer Registration under Regulation (EU) 2017/745 (MDR)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Protection Agency – Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B – Registration (Screening) typically required under the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment. A full EIA is generally not required for low-emission assembly of medical devices, but an environmental operating permit (autorisation environnementale) is mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with Luxembourg wastewater discharge limits (Règlement grand-ducal du 24 novembre 2000), emission thresholds for volatile organic compounds under Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive), and waste handling requirements under the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste. Cleanroom air filtration and microbial contamination limits per ISO 13485 and ISO 14644 standards apply to final assembly and testing areas.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) and the municipal authority, covering alarms, extinguishers, and evacuation routes; structural load inspection certificate for machinery installations; occupational health and safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) for electrical, mechanical, and ergonomic risks.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - Luxembourg Inland Revenue (portal: MyGuichet.lu and ACD 'eSpace'); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) - competent for VAT and indirect duty registration (portal: MyGuichet.lu); Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS) as the institutional front door for entity identification.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign sponsor executes the SCSp partnership agreement (private deed suffices; notarial deed optional) and files it for RCS registration; the Luxembourg Business Registers assigns the statutory 13-digit business identification number (matricule). The SCSp then files VAT application Form 1043 with the AED via MyGuichet.lu and receives the Luxembourg VAT number (TVA LU00000000). Direct-tax registration is completed through the ACD upon first lodgement of the annual transparency declaration (Form 500); no minimum capital is required and non-resident ownership is unrestricted. Non-resident partners are not separately registered for Luxembourg VAT solely because the partnership carries on taxable activities; the partnership registers and acts as a distinct taxable person for indirect tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - the SCSp is fiscally transparent for Luxembourg direct tax purposes: it is not subject to corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT), or net wealth tax (NWT); each partner is taxed directly on its pro-rata share of Luxembourg-source income. For VAT, however, the SCSp is a separate taxable person in its own name and must charge, collect, and remit Luxembourg VAT on taxable supplies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists; SCSp fiscal transparency is mandatory under Articles 104(4) and 175bis of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR) and cannot be waived. Available elections: (i) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) under Article 60 of the 1979 VAT Law, effective 1 January 2024, allowing the SCSp and its general partner to form one taxable person; (ii) optional partnership tax return (Form 500) to formalise profit allocation for non-resident partners and foreign tax credit claims; (iii) ATAD hybrid-mismatch adjustment election under the implementing Law of 20 December 2019, requiring alignment of the SCSp treatment within a 24-month window to prevent recharacterisation by the partner's tax jurisdiction; (iv) no CFC or territorial-opt-in election is available for a manufacturing SCSp.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Mandatory VAT registration applies once annual taxable turnover (VAT-exclusive) exceeds EUR 35,000; below this threshold the small-business exemption under Article 57 of the VAT Law may apply. Registration is required regardless of the threshold where the SCSp makes export supplies, makes intra-Community distance sales exceeding the EUR 10,000 annual EU-wide threshold, receives reverse-charge services, or is established outside the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a real-time transaction-level fiscal clearance, API stamping, or digital tax-stamping regime. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only to invoices addressed to Luxembourg public-sector entities (B2G), which must be transmitted in structured Peppol BIS 3.0 format. Domestic B2B e-invoicing is not yet mandatory; Luxembourg is aligning with the EU VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) framework, with mandatory B2B e-invoicing and digital transaction reporting expected by 2027 but not operational as of 2025. Export declarations are cleared electronically via the EU Export Control System (ECS); no separate VAT clearance gateway applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: The SCSp may zero-rate the sale of ICU mechanical ventilators under Article 53(1)(1) of the 1979 VAT Law where: (i) the goods are sold to a customer outside the EU; (ii) the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the EU customs territory; (iii) transport is initiated during, or within 90 days following, the time of supply; and (iv) the SCSp possesses the customs export declaration and the complete transport/commercial evidence before the VAT return is filed. Directly related offshore freight, insurance, and installation services charged on the same export invoice may also qualify for 0% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EXA/AAD export documentation issued through the EU Export Control System of the member state from which the goods physically leave)
Bill of Lading (or CMR/air waybill) evidencing the export route and exit from the EU customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (SWIFT MT103 or authenticated bank confirmation showing receipt of export proceeds from the non-EU buyer)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED treats export zero-rating as a high-risk audit channel and requires the complete export dossier at the time of filing. Export proceeds must be repatriated to the SCSp's bank account within 180 days of shipment; failure to evidence such repatriation is treated as an indicator of fictitious export and triggers reassessment of VAT at the 16% standard rate, default interest at 0.6% per month, and administrative fines of up to EUR 250,000 for serious VAT fraud cases. Retrospective clawbacks may extend to ten years where fraud is established, and criminal referral may result in imprisonment up to five years for the managing general partner and authorised signatories; fiscal transparency of the SCSp does not shield partners from intentional indirect-tax non-compliance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) operating within the Eurosystem; competences shared with the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy and with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking supervision and AML/CFT enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Eurozone member state: the euro is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. There are no exchange control approvals, no restrictions on inward direct investment, and no barriers to profit or dividend repatriation under the EU free movement of capital (Article 63 TFEU). The tax-transparent SCSp may receive capital contributions from non-resident partners and remit profits freely; non-resident limited partners are not subject to Luxembourg income tax on distributions except where profits are attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment under the Luxembourg Income Tax Law (LIR). Practical hurdles are limited to AML/KYC documentation, CRS/FATCA registration, and BCL balance-of-payments statistical reporting by the resident bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, forced conversion, or holding-period obligation on export proceeds. Exports of ICU mechanical ventilators are subject to EU medical-device regulation (EU 2017/745) and CE marking; export receipts in any currency may be retained onshore or offshore in any bank account. Banks apply standard transaction monitoring and may require underlying sale contracts, customs declarations, and purchase orders to evidence the commercial nature of incoming funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Compte Séquestre) and Operational Current Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Current Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Current Account
Operational Current Account and FX-Hedging Margin Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low for primary treasury function. Luxembourg-licensed electronic money institutions under PSD2/CSSF supervision may open accounts for an SCSp, but they cannot provide trade finance, government LC confirmation, or correspondent-banking rails for LC-backed ventilator tenders. Offshore digital EMIs are generally rejected for this structure because they lack access to TARGET2, cannot settle BCL-reportable capital flows, and most Tier-1 Luxembourg banks refuse to recognize them as banking counterparties under CSSF AML/CFT guidance. Feasibility: Low; at most an ancillary collection account for customer receivables forwarded to a fully licensed domestic bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is legally permissible under Luxembourg AML law using CSSF-approved video identification or certification by a Luxembourg notary or regulated audit firm; however, in practice Tier-1 banks require at least one in-person signatory meeting for the general partner's authorized managers and all beneficial owners. Non-EU directors may rely on a video interview supported by apostilled corporate documents and a local Luxembourg registered agent or notary physically attending the bank; a full notarized power of attorney in English, French, or German is required when no director appears.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp default lack of legal personality and unlimited liability of the general partner raise compliance doubts on entity capacity and signing power.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and translated partnership agreement; RCSL registration certificate and published e-filing in the Recueil électronique des sociétés; RBE beneficial-ownership register extract; legal opinion of Luxembourg counsel confirming the capacity and representation of the general partner; board resolution appointing authorized signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident ownership with a multi-tier or offshore holding chain triggers enhanced due diligence on UBO identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated RBE filing; corporate organizational chart traced to natural persons; passport copies of all UBOs; certified source-of-wealth and source-of-funds report; audited financial statements of the direct investor for the last three years; tax residence certificates for each entity in the ownership chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent pass-through classification may be misread as an unregulated collective investment vehicle or trigger FATCA/CRS reporting risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg tax confirmation letter or ruling confirming SCSp tax transparency; CRS/FATCA registration certificate; DAC6 report-ready intercompany documentation; business plan proving active commercial manufacturing rather than passive investment holding.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Life-support medical device manufacturing and government-tender receipts attract sanctions, export-control, and procurement-fraud screening alerts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CE certificate under EU MDR 2017/745 with Notified Body report; Luxembourg Ministry of Health manufacturing authorization; export declarations and license confirmations; original purchase orders or tenders from foreign public health authorities; WHO prequalification or FDA registration, if applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large capital injection from foreign limited partners with no prior banking track record flags potential money-laundering or unsecured-lending risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized subscription and capital-call agreements; bank reference letters from contributing partners; source-of-funds statement with supporting account statements; sworn declaration that funds derive from legitimate commercial operations; undertaking to provide periodic capital-call and audited financial reports.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Contributions are remitted via SWIFT MT103 from the limited partner's bank to the SCSp euro operating account at the Luxembourg bank, using ISO purpose code CAPC (capital payment) and a mandatory payment reference including the SCSp name and RCSL number. The Luxembourg bank records the inflow for BCL balance-of-payments statistics; no prior central bank authorization is required. For euro transfers originating within SEPA, an SEPA Credit Transfer is accepted, but the payment must clearly reference the specific capital-call notice; the bank may pre-screen the RBE status and may require a written escrow release instruction before funds move from the capital escrow account to the operating account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail is a commercial letter of credit governed by UCP 600, issued or confirmed by the buyer's bank under SWIFT MT700/MT707; settlement on presentation of compliant documents is effected through TARGET2 in euro or via SWIFT MT103/MT202 in foreign currency. Supplier and operational disbursements use SWIFT MT103 with ISO purpose codes SUPP (supplier payment) or TRAD (trade payment). Disbursement verification requires commercial invoice, airway bill or bill of lading, CE certificate, certificate of origin, inspection report, and government-endorsed acceptance certificate for ICU ventilator deliveries.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla EUR/USD and EUR/GBP deliverable forwards under an ISDA FX Master Agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD settled in euro where the buyer's central bank restricts currency conversion
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD) matching the tenor of government procurement receivables
FX swaps for short-term rolling of foreign-currency contract balances
Zero-cost FX collars combining a USD call/EUR put with a USD put/EUR call

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts of the SCSp under Luxembourg GAAP filed with the RCS; filing generally not mandatory for an SCSp without legal personality, but required where the partnership agreement, a financing agreement, or a public-tender/government-procurement contract (including ICU ventilator supply) stipulates accounts.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg; e-filed via RCS/eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Approval by the general partner no later than 6 months after the balance-sheet date and filing with RCS within 1 month after approval; for a calendar-year financial year ending 31 December, the operative latest filing date is 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If the SCSp becomes obliged to file, late or omitted filing is sanctioned by RCS civil fines up to EUR 5,000, publication of the omission, and, for persistent non-compliance, possible judicial winding-up or strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-owner declaration and update in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), operated by the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No annual fixed date; initial declaration on incorporation and any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days of the event. Annual year-end review is recommended to confirm accuracy.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or untimely update of RBE data is a criminal offence carrying fines of up to EUR 1,250,000 for legal entities and, for individuals, fines and imprisonment up to 5 years; responsible partners may also be debarred.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual tax information return of the fiscally transparent SCSp (partnership return) and individual/partner allocable income declarations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a financial year ending 31 December, the partnership return is due by 31 December of the following year; an automatic extension for e-filers generally grants 31 March, and professional practitioners may obtain a further extension to 31 May.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on the tax assessed (minimum EUR 1,500), monthly late-payment interest at 0.6%, and additional administrative penalties up to EUR 10,000 for repeated default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual employer social-security declaration (déclaration annuelle des salaires) covering all employees engaged in the ventilator-manufacturing activity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 1 February following the remuneration year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late submission exposes the SCSp/employer to administrative fines, surcharges up to EUR 20,000, and liability for unpaid employer and employee social contributions with statutory interest.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent audit by a Luxembourg-approved réviseur d'entreprises agréé is compulsory if the SCSp exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds in two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average workforce 50 employees. A CSSF-regulated SCSp used as an AIF is always subject to periodic audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (as codified in the Law of 19 December 2002 on the accounting obligations of undertakings, as amended); IFRS/EU-IFRS is available for voluntary consolidated financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg's RBE law requires the SCSp to file an initial beneficial-owner declaration on RCS registration and to notify any change in beneficial ownership within 30 days. There is no annual re-filing calendar date; however, the general partner should conduct and document an annual UBO confirmation as of the 31 December year-end to maintain current, accurate RBE records and to support any transactional disclosures to banks or procurement counterparties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners and Partnership Interests
Register of Partnership Decisions / General Partner Resolution Book
Statutory Accounting Books and Supporting Contracts
Register of Employees (with employment declarations if staff engaged)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% CIT on taxable profits exceeding EUR 175,000 (15% on the first EUR 175,000), plus a 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax, producing an aggregate Luxembourg City headline rate of up to 24.94% for taxable entities; an SCSp is ordinarily fiscally transparent and is not itself subject to CIT unless the structure is recharacterised as commercially taxable.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp profits are allocated to partners and taxed at partner level; no manufacturing-sector tax holiday applies, but qualifying IP income may benefit from the Luxembourg IP regime (80% exemption, producing an effective rate of about 5%), and participation exemption applies to qualifying dividends and capital gains.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined annual corporate tax return for CIT, municipal business tax (MBT) and net wealth tax (NWT) on Formulaire 510, filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu / the Luxembourg direct tax e-filing portal (ESIS).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally, for calendar-year taxpayers, the filing deadline is 30 June of the year following the fiscal year-end; the Administration des contributions directes commonly grants extensions to 31 December upon reasoned electronic request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCS Luxembourg registration number, registered office, legal form code (SCSp), Luxembourg tax file number, fiscal year-end and contact details of the authorised representative.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the SCSp's Luxembourg registered address, designate a Luxembourg tax representative if no local manager is present, and list all non-resident partners separately with country of residence and any Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE) indicator.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the SCSp is fiscally transparent, that no opaque entity election has been made, and that the partnership does not itself carry on activities requiring a Luxembourg corporate profit tax filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident general partners must certify whether the SCSp's manufacturing and trading activities create a Luxembourg PE; if a PE exists, the partner's allocable profits are subject to Luxembourg CIT/MBT filing obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit or loss from manufacturing turbine-driven critical care invasive ventilators, reconciled to Luxembourg GAAP financial statements and including inventory, gross margin, depreciation, warranty and government procurement revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners without a PE should report only Luxembourg-source income; losses allocated to non-residents may be deferred if not itemised in the Luxembourg return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-back of non-deductible expenses, including excessive interest, payments to fully transparent or tax-haven entities without economic substance, fines, penalties, lobbying costs, and gratuitous asset transfers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses borne directly by the foreign partner are not deductible at the SCSp level unless incurred for the benefit of and through the Luxembourg PE; attach an expense allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1c / Participation exemption and IP box deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduct qualifying tax-exempt dividends and capital gains from substantial EU or treaty participations, and deduct 80% of net qualifying IP income attributable to patents, copyrighted software and equivalent IP assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must provide documentary evidence of qualifying participation status and IP ownership; assets must be economically owned and managed in Luxembourg.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 / Taxable income or allocable loss
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed taxable result after reserves, recharging adjustments, loss carryforward deductions and available tax credits; disclose any profit distribution anticipated for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A valid nil return must still be filed in every year; attach partner allocation statements showing the profit/loss percentage attributed to each non-resident partner.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is subject to administrative fines up to EUR 25,000, a late-filing surcharge of up to 10% of the assessed tax, and monthly default interest of approximately 0.8% on unpaid CIT/MBT. Persistent failure allows ex officio assessment and criminal prosecution for tax evasion, exposing the entity to fines up to EUR 500,000 and imprisonment of responsible managers up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a Luxembourg resident taxable company; an SCSp is fiscally transparent, so ordinary profit distributions to partners are generally not treated as Luxembourg-source dividends at the partnership level. Where a taxable Luxembourg underlying company pays dividends, the 15% rate may be reduced to 0% or 5% under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive or an applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply for DTA relief, the beneficial owner must obtain a valid Luxembourg tax residence certificate if the payer is treaty-reliant, submit a properly executed withholding-tax relief form/affidavit to the paying agent, provide beneficial ownership and shareholding evidence (holding percentage, holding period and substantive operations), and, if full 15% was withheld, file a refund claim with the Administration des contributions directes within five years from the date of payment. In an SCSp, treaty benefits require the partners to be the actual owners of the income and to demonstrate commercial substance beyond the partnership vehicle.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law generally imposes no withholding tax on royalties or interest paid by a Luxembourg taxable entity to non-residents, except for certain savings-income payments to individuals. Consequently, most DTA-credentialed non-resident recipients benefit from a 0% effective rate; the payer must still document the beneficial owner's identity with a TRC and beneficial-ownership confirmation to avoid administrative recharacterisation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File and Country-by-Country Report: group consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000. Local File: local net turnover above EUR 50,000,000 or a Luxembourg entity engaged in material related-party transactions with non-residents; prudent contemporaneous documentation is required where related-party intercompany flows exceed EUR 500,000 in aggregate, and always for the ventilator distribution/royalty chains.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no formal Economic Substance Regulations statute analogous to offshore regimes, but EU ATAD GAAR, the Luxembourg General Tax Law and case-law require genuine economic substance for the SCSp to be recognised as transparent and to access treaty benefits. Acceptable substance evidence includes local registered office, active and qualified management, local bank account, board minutes, risk control, controlled manufacturing or procurement activity, payroll and operational expenditure in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of taxable profits through fictitious ventilator-component invoices, off-book government procurement cash, unreported rebates, or concealed related-party manufacturing fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg General Tax Law penalties for intentional tax evasion may reach three times the evaded tax; criminal fines may reach EUR 500,000 and imprisonment up to five years for accountable managers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and SCSp managers who sign false declarations or knowingly implement sham invoicing can be jointly and severally liable for the entity's CIT, MBT, NWT, interest and penalties; courts may impose travel bans, passport seizures, asset freezes and dismissal disqualification.
